normalization.overview: Nate Herk argues that cache invalidation, oversized sessions and unnecessary global instructions consume agent usage. GhostMesh investigates four layers of reuse and the actual economics of accepted outcomes.
normalization.whyItMatters: Provider caching, active working context, source evidence and governed memory have different validity and cost boundaries.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Preserve the minimum sufficient currently authorized state, measure accepted outcomes, version evidence and keep capability discovery durable.
normalization.falsification: Compare a representative read-only evidence-reconstruction task across baseline, stable-prefix and versioned evidence reuse; record acceptance, sources, costs, latency, freshness and authorization changes.
normalization.freshness: Video November 22, 2026; official provider sources verified in the November 23 evidence registry and rechecked November 24. Metrics illustrative; creator anecdotes not independently verified.

relationships.reason: examines the operational failure to discover an existing tool. This Reader extends that concern into the cost of repetitive inference and evidence retrieval, and shows why a registered pointer must be consumed in a real task.

challenges the assumption that more instructions and capabilities necessarily improve work. Together they expose the tension between shrinking working context and maintaining the discoverability of rare but consequential procedures.
distinguishes candidate-answer pricing from the cost of accepted work. It is the closest economic companion to the cache and compaction examples here.
